name: momentum_reversion_switch_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Intraday markets alternate between momentum and mean-reversion regimes. During high-ADX periods (ADX(14) > 25), trend-following via EMA crossover outperforms. During low-ADX periods (ADX(14) < 18), Bollinger Band mean-reversion dominates. The inefficiency arises because most strategies are static — they commit to one paradigm and suffer during the wrong regime. By using ADX as a real-time regime classifier and switching between two sub-strategies, we capture edge in both states. This is not arbitraged away because the switching cost and model complexity deter simpler algos, and the regime transitions are noisy enough that classification accuracy is imperfect.
mechanism: Short-term selling exhausts available demand at a price level, creating a temporary liquidity vacuum. Market makers who absorbed the selling begin marking prices back to reduce inventory risk. Limit buy orders resting below create a floor, and new participants entering the long side accelerate the reversion as the forced selling pressure dissipates.

conditions: MOMENTUM_REGIME: ADX(14) > 25 AND EMA(close,9) crosses above EMA(close,21) AND close > vwap
REVERSION_REGIME: ADX(14) < 18 AND close < BB_lower AND close < vwap
MOMENTUM_REGIME: ADX(14) > 25 AND EMA(close,9) crosses below EMA(close,21) AND close < vwap
REVERSION_REGIME: ADX(14) < 18 AND close > BB_upper AND close > vwap

exit.signal_exit: Regime switch (ADX crosses threshold) triggers immediate exit

filters.vix_filter: No filter — strategy is regime-adaptive by design
filters.volume_filter: Stock must have traded > 500 shares in last 5 bars

weaknesses: ADX(14) on 1-min bars takes ~28 bars to stabilize, losing the first 30 minutes of trading session to indicator warm-up
Regime classification in the ADX 18-25 'dead zone' is ambiguous — neither sub-strategy performs well, leading to whipsaws
Switching cost: each regime transition requires closing existing position and potentially reversing, doubling transaction costs during choppy transitions
prior_art: Ang & Timmermann (2012) regime-switching models; Kole & van Dijk (2017) on Markov-switching for trading; ADX regime classification is common in technical analysis literature
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
